findings.title: Retry-count deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch matches only `retryCount > 1` and does not require `method: SMS`, `scheduled: false`, or a future/past scheduledDate. This SMS cron therefore deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows as well whenever their retryCount exceeds 1, even though it never attempted to schedule them and their own handlers may still need them. The retry cleanup should be restricted to the unscheduled SMS reminders this job actually retries.

findings.title: Retry-count update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without its own error handling. If that update fails — for example the row was deleted by a concurrent cron invocation (Prisma P2025) or the original error was a transient database failure — the new exception escapes the catch, terminates the for loop, and the handler returns an error instead of processing the remaining unscheduled reminders. One bad reminder can therefore block all later reminders in the run; the increment should be best-effort or use a delete/updateMany that tolerates a missing row.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or no message never get a retry count
findings.body: Retry counting only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` (via the scheduledSMS-null branch) or in the catch block. A reminder whose booking has no `smsReminderNumber`, whose workflow step has no `sendTo`, or whose message resolves to empty silently falls through with retryCount unchanged and `scheduled` still false, so it is re-fetched and re-processed on every cron invocation until its scheduledDate finally passes — exactly the endless-rescheduling loop this PR is meant to eliminate for undeliverable SMS reminders.

findings.title: Retry count is written from a stale read instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both retry writes set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both read the same retryCount (e.g. 1), both fail, and both write 2's predecessor value 2-minus-one (i.e. both write 2 when starting from 1 is fine, but starting from 0 both write 1), so failed attempts are under-counted and the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold can be postponed indefinitely under repeated overlap. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update instead.
